stem.text: The power series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{\left(x - 1\right)^{n}}{5^{n} n^{\frac{3}{2}}} \) has radius of convergence \( 5 \). Determine whether the series converges or diverges at \( x = 6 \), naming the test used.

answer_key.label: At \( x = 6 \) the series converges by the p-series test, because \( p = \frac{3}{2} > 1 \).

worked_solution.text: The ratio test gives convergence for \( \left|x - 1\right| < 5 \), so the right endpoint is \( x = 6 \).
At \( x = 6 \), \( \frac{\left(x - 1\right)^{n}}{5^{n}} = \left(\frac{5}{5}\right)^{n} = 1 \), so the series becomes \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{\frac{3}{2}}} \).
It is a p-series with \( p = \frac{3}{2} > 1 \).
At \( x = 6 \) the series converges by the p-series test, because \( p = \frac{3}{2} > 1 \), so \( x = 6 \) belongs to the interval of convergence.

options.label: At \( x = 6 \) the series converges by the p-series test, because \( p = \frac{3}{2} > 1 \).
At \( x = 6 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because the sizes \( \frac{1}{n^{\frac{3}{2}}} \) decrease to 0.
options.derivation: the alternating series test used on the endpoint series although its terms are all positive

options.label: At \( x = 6 \) the series diverges by the p-series test, because \( p = \frac{3}{2} > 1 \).
options.derivation: the p-series threshold reversed, so p greater than 1 read as divergence

options.label: At \( x = 6 \) the series diverges by the ratio test, because \( -4 < x < 6 \) leaves it out.
options.derivation: the endpoint never examined: the open interval from the ratio test taken as the whole answer
